risks: Minimal: secondary use of de-identified logs. The main risk is blaming individual technologists for system delays; results are reported by shift and location, never by staff member.
consent: Waiver of consent approved by the research ethics board for de-identified secondary use (REB file 26-311).
data: The extract contains no names or record numbers, only a study identifier, location type, clinic area and times; it is held on the laboratory's secure server and destroyed five years after publication.
equity: PROGRESS-Plus: patients of community clinics, many in outlying and lower-income areas, and patients whose results are verified at night carry most of the delay. Results are reported by clinic area and time block so that an escalation route can be targeted to them.
effectiveness: The review shows whether delays are concentrated where an escalation route or night staffing change would act.
efficiency: Existing data and 60 hours of analysis.
partnerships: Laboratory information system manager (extract), community clinic network lead (on-call lists), two technologists who work nights (interpretation), and one patient partner from the hospital's patient council.
rebPath: Approved by the research ethics board with a waiver of consent (REB file 26-311, 2026-08-27); data access agreed under LIS-DR-2026-19.
limitations: Call logs record documentation, not clinical action; roster data may not show informal help at night; patient outcomes are not measured.
summary: Approved secondary use with a waiver, system-level reporting, and equity reporting for community and night results.
